author: Alex Berger
title: Dog Days of Summer event in Colonie fundraises for local veterinarian - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Berger ,
1 hours ago
COLONIE, N.Y. ( WTEN ) -- The dog days of summer are named for the hot, humid days of August. But the Colonie Police Department had a perfect day Wednesday to host a dog filled afternoon in support of a local veterinarian.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! At Cook Park, four-legged friends were the center of attention, especially with it being National Dog Day. Money raised at the event through donations went towards the Boght Veterinary Clinic and Dr. David Wagoner, who does so much work in the community.
"Any time we have a lost dog, abandoned dog, our officers get a call for it," said Matthew Stott, a school resource officer with the Colonie Police. "[If] we can't find an owner, [Wagoner will] take that dog in, provide whatever medical care is needed, and work with a lot of the rescues that we have here this afternoon to find the temporary and eventually permanent housing for those animals."
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Festivities included a pet parade, a costume contest and a talent show. For rescue groups, it was an opportunity to showcase their services.
Gianna Ciccone, a community outreach manager for the Mohawk Hudson Humane Society , highlighted the shelter's program called Loved for Life . It allows the owners of pets who qualify to get free pet food, low-cost vaccinations for their pet along with income qualified spay and neuter surgeries.
Right now, the humane society has a promotion going on called "Clear the Shelters." This means their adoption fees for dogs and cats are 60% off. It's to find dogs and cats their forever homes, as the shelter has just about reached their limit on intakes.
"At the shelter right now, I believe we're housing close to 90 dogs," said Ciccone. "Cats, I think, is somewhere close to 80. So we are at pretty much maximum capacity as far as dogs and cats."
A non-profit called Out of the Pits , just like its namesake, spreads positivity about Pitbulls. Since 1994, they've also helped find dogs a place to live, being able to rehome more than 3,000 dogs since their organization's founding.
"We like to bring community awareness to pit bulls," said volunteer Gabrielle Hogan. "We do a lot of fostering, so animals that need places of homes. We help people find their dream dogs."
The dog days of summer are almost over, but the need to help animals remains year round.
"Dog owners, I think, kind of all have that bond that they like dogs and they like to stick together," said Stott. "People also like being part of a community and giving back, and this is our way to do it, especially at a real local level, so they know all the donations are going and staying right here in the town of Colonie."
